reason: council-remediation-2026-07-20 agent-R: original question cited 'R-1/R-2/R-3/R-4/R-5 lot abutment rules' that do not appear in PD 1096 Sec. 704 (PD 1096 uses Group A-B-C-D occupancy classifications, not US-style R-1 to R-5 zoning). Replaced with a Sec. 704 firewall/zero-lot-line wall question that the article directly supports.

source_audit_support.citation: PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Rule VII, Section 704.4

proposed.text: Under PD 1096 Rule VII Section 704, when a building is constructed with its exterior wall directly on a side or rear property line (zero setback on that side), what opening and wall requirement applies to that wall?

options.text: The wall must be constructed as a firewall with no unprotected openings permitted at zero setback from the property line
Openings are permitted up to 50 percent of the wall area as long as fire-rated glazing is used
Openings are permitted up to 25 percent of the wall area, with no special fire-rating required
Openings are unrestricted because zero-setback walls are governed by local zoning, not PD 1096

proposed.rationale: A wall built on the property line presents maximum fire-spread risk to the adjacent property. Section 704 therefore requires the wall to be a firewall, and no unprotected openings are permitted in an exterior wall located at zero setback from the property line.
proposed.explanation: This is the strictest end of the Section 704 opening-protection scheme. As the wall moves away from the property line, protected openings become permitted, and the familiar 50 percent protected-opening cap per storey applies within the applicable distance band.
